set_text.text: What counts as a procurement saving?

A procurement saving is money a negotiation takes off what you pay suppliers, measured from a baseline price. A hard saving lowers the price on the invoice. Cost avoidance stops a rise that was on its way. Both count, but only the first shows up in spend.
Lower prices on cases you were already buying, on the same terms. A new line has no old price to beat, so its first price is spend, not a saving.
Rebates paid back later, better payment terms and free goods. Each can be worth real money, but each belongs on its own line, not in the case price.
You resell what you buy. If the $1.44 a case goes straight into lower sell prices, your accounts keep the saving and your margin stays put.
Who uses a procurement savings calculator
It is for independent food distributors whose buyers negotiate supplier prices. Anyone who reports a saving, checks one or signs off a renewal should run it.
